description: baseline

Bottleneck: compute throughput at large n (shapes 4,5,6: n=1024/2048/4096). FP32 SIMT leaves BF16 tensor cores (~2 PFLOP/s) idle. Implement blocked Householder QR whose panel and trailing updates use BF16/FP16 tensor-core GEMM (WMMA or cublas) with FP32 accumulation, exploiting the loose factor tolerance (20*n*eps32 ~1e-2 at n=4096). Add one FP32 correction sweep if orthogonality fails. Produce valid H/tau.
PyTorch blocked Householder QR (WY block reflectors, BLK=64); validates all 19 shapes FP32; shape3 5.1x faster but geomean 139417us slower overall due to per-column launch overhead at large n
Fused CUDA panel kernel (1 block/matrix) + TF32 trailing update; orthogonality perfect but factor residual fails band/rowscale n=512 (scaled 26-28 vs 20); pure-FP32 trailing passes all 19

3xTF32 split trailing update (near-FP32 on tensor cores); passes all 19. Geomean 54298us. Shape3 640x512 8.7x faster, n=176/352/1024 2-2.6x faster; n=2048/4096 5.6x/29x slower (panel kernel 1 block/matrix underutilizes GPU at batch 2/8)

Recursive panel: width-64 split to base-16 per-column kernel, inter-half block-reflector applies via 3xTF32 GEMM. Passes all 19. Geomean 26284us = 1.70x vs baseline. n=512 batch640 20.7x, n=1024 4.6x; n=2048 0.53x, n=4096 0.11x (3x better than iter3)

Cooperative-grid panel kernel for batch<=32 (row-reductions across many blocks, grid.sync between columns). Passes all 19 but grid-sync overhead dominates: geomean 32594us (regression vs iter4 26284). s5 144->257ms, s6 474->571ms. Reverting default to recursive next; base-case kernel efficiency is the better lever

Optimized base panel kernel: fused trailing-column dot products (one pass, register accumulators), warp-shuffle reductions, fused larft. Coop disabled. Passes all 19. Geomean 20036us = 2.23x vs baseline. All shapes improved: s3 43.2ms, s4 43ms, s5 102ms, s6 305ms

Adaptive base width: min(32,n) for n<=256 else 16 (recursion-overhead vs serial-work tradeoff). Added _PREC 1/2/3 modes (2 fails, 3xTF32 default). Passes all 19. Geomean 18073us = 2.47x vs baseline; s0 327 s1 3437 (small shapes much better), large unchanged
torch.geqrf fallback for batch<32 & n>1024 (cuSOLVER beats our panel there). s5 102->77ms s6 306->54ms (both =baseline floor). Custom keeps s0-s4. Passes all 19. Geomean 13474us = 3.32x vs baseline

Shared-memory base panel kernel: caches whole base panel in smem (opt-in ~160KB), all columns in shared, write back once. Eliminates global re-reads (was 47% of s3). Passes all 19. s3 43.3->35.9ms (29.9x baseline), s4 43.5->37.8ms (6.4x). Geomean 12551us = 3.56x vs baseline

Cut torch overhead: reuse V TF32-split across both products + recursion; subtract trailing update in-place on strided H view (no copy-back). Passes all 19. s3 35.9->33.8ms, s4 37.8->36.0ms. Geomean 12189us = 3.67x vs baseline

Tried direct full-width smem panel for batch>=256 (no recursion): regression s3 33.8->83.8ms (1 block/SM + serial 64-col chain loses to recursion's parallel GEMM). Reverted; fixed smem-size bug. Back to 12169us. Lesson: recursion+tensor-core GEMM beats wide serial panel at all batch sizes
Smem base kernel emits unit-lower V directly at writeback -> skips host tril/arange/index + a copy. Passes all 19. All shapes down: s2 8.2->6.9ms, s4 36->32.9ms. Geomean 11374us = 3.93x vs baseline

Pad shared panel leading dim to bb+1 -> eliminates 2-way bank conflicts in column reductions. Big win: s3 32.6->27.9ms (38.6x baseline), s4 29.4ms, s0/s1/s2 down. Passes all 19. Geomean 10380us = 4.31x vs baseline
Base width 32 in custom path (bank-fixed kernel makes wide base win): halves recursion depth -> less glue. s4 29.4->25.3ms, s2 6.5->5.3ms, s3 26.5ms. Passes all 19. Geomean 9807us = 4.56x vs baseline
Panel threads 256->128 (latency-bound kernel: 128 gives better occupancy). Swept 64/128/256/512, 128 wins. s3 25.5ms. Passes all 19. Geomean 9644us = 4.64x vs baseline

Tried single-TF32 for the middle T^T W1 / T@cross products (save 2 GEMMs/update). Fails band/rowscale (scaled 23-24 vs 20): W1=V^T C carries wide data dynamic range, rounding it to TF32 loses too much. Reverting; middle product needs >=2-term precision on W1

2-GEMM T^T W1 (T unsplit/clean, W1 split for its data dynamic range) vs 3xTF32: saves 1 GEMM+1 split per trailing update, passes all 19 (single-TF32 failed). s3 24.9ms, s2 5.0ms. Geomean 9471us = 4.72x vs baseline

Brief #0 (large-n tensor-core blocked Householder QR) exhaustively explored over 17 iterations: baseline 44710us -> 9471us local (4.72x). On the GPU MODE leaderboard this reached RANK 6 (5810us); the gap to #1 (2707us) shrank from 7.35x at start to ~2.15x. All 19 test shapes pass; remote submissions accepted (not flagged as cheating). Final = commit 65afe59.

WORKING DESIGN: right-looking blocked Householder QR returning genuine compact (H,tau). Orthogonality is automatic (reflectors stay FP32-clean); only the factor residual is precision-sensitive and the loose tol (20*n*eps32) admits reduced precision. Trailing/inter-half updates run as 3xTF32 split GEMMs (hi@hi+hi@lo+lo@hi) on tensor cores = near-FP32, passing all stress cases. Panel = custom CUDA, one block/matrix, recursive (base width 32) with GEMM inter-half applies. Low-batch large-n (s5 b8 n2048, s6 b2 n4096) routed to torch.geqrf.

KEY WINS (in impact order): recursive panel + GEMM applies (1.70x); optimized base kernel - fused multi-column dot-products + warp-shuffle reductions (2.23x); adaptive base width (2.47x); geqrf fallback for low-batch large-n (3.32x); shared-memory base-panel caching (3.56x); kernel emits unit-lower V directly, skips host tril/index (3.93x); PADDED shared leading dim bb+1 to kill bank conflicts (4.31x, panel 350->202us/call); base width 32 halving recursion depth (4.56x); 128 panel threads for occupancy (4.64x); 2-GEMM T^T W1 - T unsplit/clean, W1 split (4.72x).

DEAD ENDS (logged): BF16 trailing fails band/rowscale factor check (scaled 26-50 vs 20); single-TF32 and both 2-term splits fail (small-n needs V split, stress needs C split -> all 3 terms required for V^T C); cooperative-grid panel kernel - per-column grid.sync overhead exceeds parallelism gain; direct full-width-64 smem panel - serial 64-col chain on 1 block/matrix loses to recursion+GEMM even at batch 640.

Per-shape ratios vs baseline (local): s0(n32 b20)=1.4x, s1(n176 b40)=9x, s2(n352 b40)=10x, s3(n512 b640)=43x, s4(n1024 b60)=9.5x, s5/s6=1.0x (cuSOLVER floor). s3 is the dominant absolute time; s5+s6 are the geomean anchors stuck at cuSOLVER parity.

PROVEN: beating cuSOLVER on s5/s6 is impractical with this approach - at batch 2/8 the problem is too small to fill tensor cores (my custom: s5 107ms, s6 454ms vs cuSOLVER 77ms/54ms). cuSOLVER parallelizes its panel intra-matrix; my one-block-per-matrix panel can't, and the cooperative alternative is sync-bound.

SUGGESTED FRESH BRIEFS:
1) (HIGHEST VALUE) s5/s6 are the two geomean anchors at 1.0x; the leaders almost certainly beat cuSOLVER here. Needs a DIFFERENT low-batch large-n algorithm: communication-avoiding TSQR panel, or an intra-matrix-parallel panel that avoids grid.sync (e.g. split-K reductions with a 2-kernel handshake), or recover Householder (H,tau) cheaply from a CholeskyQR2 Q,R. Unlocking 1.5-3x on s5/s6 -> ~5.5-6x overall.
2) s3 panel kernel is ~46% of its time even at base32; a warp-specialized / double-buffered panel or a smaller-base+larger-tile recursion could shave it.
3) BF16/FP16 multi-pass split for the trailing GEMM (BF16 throughput ~2x TF32): risky (BF16 split ~14 mantissa bits, borderline for stress) but its own brief could establish whether 3xBF16-split passes and beats 3xTF32.

R=triu(U_p^T A) FAILS the LAPACK factor gate by 25-142x at every shape. Confirmed even with an EXACT FP64-SVD polar (s3 cond2 129x, cond0 407x; ||U_p - Q_qr||=37) AND across NS it=5/6/8 (orth converges to ~1x but factor stays 25-142x over the gate). QR's Q triangularizes A; the polar Q does not -- they are different orthogonal matrices.
2) THE VALID ALL-GEMM ALTERNATIVE (CholeskyQR2: G=A^TA, R=chol, Q=A R^-1, x2) IS ALREADY 2.0-6.4x SLOWER than the champion's WHOLE per-shape time BEFORE any recon. So 'all-tensor-core fills better than the panel' is FALSE here -- the champion's panel Householder is already the more efficient structure at s3/s4.
3) THE RECON MOAT is mandatory and catastrophic. The checker rebuilds Q=householder_product(H,tau) ITSELF (reference.py L144) and ignores any explicit Q, so ANY explicit-Q method (polar OR CQR2) must orhr_col-recon Q->compact(H,tau). Measured tax: 8.0ms (s5) to 110ms (s3); CQR2+recon TOTAL = 4.0-33.5x the champion per-shape.
